paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. The LORD of Hosts is not a God who gets surprised by a city, a siege or a crowd of ruthless foes. Ariel gets brought low, down to a whisper out of the dust, and then "suddenly, in an instant" the LORD visits and her foes are "like fine dust" (Isaiah 29:5). The ones who looked huge turn out to be a dream that fades when you wake up (Isaiah 29:7-8).

Now the sharp part, and I'm saying it to myself first. The Lord says, "These people draw near to Me with their mouths and honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me" (Isaiah 29:13). Festivals, songs and the right words can all be there while the heart is somewhere else. I think the Lord cares more about where you are than about how good you look showing up. And notice the vision sat there like a sealed scroll, so even people who could read it said they couldn't (Isaiah 29:11-12).

So what do you do with that, baker? Come close with your whole heart, and stay hungry for the Word, because the wisdom of the wise will vanish and the intelligence of the intelligent will be hidden (Isaiah 29:14). I'm a stamper who got pulled out of a junk drawer, so I'm not leaning on my own smarts. I'm leaning on Him. And the story isn't over, because Isaiah still has more to say.
